author: Independent education critic: fresh Claude subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) with no authoring context, launched by crewmate pep-java-installing-design-followup; not the page author

findings.claim: The module lab's Prerequisites send learners who lack the toolchain to a section named 'Now install on your own computer' that 'has numbered steps for macOS, Linux and Windows'. On the current page that heading is 'Now set up your own computer' and it now links to the vendor guides rather than giving per-OS steps, so the hand-off from lab to setup names a heading that does not exist and promises content the page no longer has.
findings.recommendation: In the same module branch, update the lab README to name the heading 'Now set up your own computer' and describe it accurately (architecture check, links to the official Temurin, Maven and IntelliJ IDEA guides, then the three checks), and rebind any lab critic or solved-run evidence that hashes the README.

findings.claim: Step 3 'Install Maven' is the one step the learner must do by hand on every OS, yet it has no completion check (unlike step 2's 'Done when the installer finishes without an error'), and the linked Maven guide only says to add the bin directory to PATH without saying how on Windows. The cheat-sheet note on line 645 then states that 'the Maven guide's PATH step set[s] PATH and JAVA_HOME' on Windows, which overstates what that guide does (it sets neither; only the Temurin MSI can set JAVA_HOME). A Windows novice reaches the hardest action with no actionable route and a misleading reassurance; the troubleshooting line 'repeat the guide's PATH step' points back to the same gap.

evidence.section: Installing Apache Maven: binary distribution, add the bin directory to PATH, confirm with mvn -v

findings.recommendation: Keep the vendor link, but add a 'Done when' for step 3 (for example: the extracted folder contains bin/mvn, and mvn -v runs in a new terminal), give a one-line pointer to where PATH is edited on Windows (or say explicitly to ask the instructor if that is unfamiliar), and correct the cheat-sheet sentence so only the Temurin installer is said to set JAVA_HOME.

findings.claim: The derived Markdown text alternative drops every link URL. Under the product decision the vendor links are now the real-machine install instructions, so a learner using artifact.md sees 'follow the guide for your system: macOS .pkg, Windows .msi ... or Linux packages' and 'Follow Installing Apache Maven' with no address to follow, and the Sources list likewise has titles only. The text alternative therefore cannot carry o1's real-machine path.
findings.recommendation: Make the derivation keep link targets (for example Markdown [text](url)) at least in the recap's setup checklist and the Sources list, then regenerate artifact.md; if this is repository-wide derivation behaviour, fix it on a tooling branch and regenerate this companion afterwards.

findings.claim: In artifact.md the two Activity hints ('Where to act: The command line of Ana's practice terminal...', 'Where to act: The two option groups...') are emitted under the '## Cheat sheet' heading, ahead of the table, without saying which activity they belong to, and the tasks themselves ('Your task' text for each activity) are absent, so the hints read as orphaned cheat-sheet entries.
findings.recommendation: Emit each hint with its activity (or drop hints from the cheat-sheet section) so the companion's cheat sheet contains only the table and its note.

findings.claim: Activity 2 step 4 says 'A failed command shows the real bash error'. The terminal is a simulation (stated in its title bar and caption) and an unsupported command prints 'not available in this practice terminal', which is not a bash error; the wording slightly overclaims fidelity in an otherwise honest simulation notice.
findings.recommendation: Say 'shows the error bash would print' and mention that only which, echo, export, ls, java, javac and mvn are available here.

items.note: Resolved under the course owner's product decision. The original defect was that the page practised only PATH repair on a fictional machine and gave no real-machine route to a working JDK 25 and Maven before the lab. The current recap section 'Now set up your own computer' (lines 622-641) gives four numbered steps: find the architecture per OS with concrete UI locations and uname -m; choose JDK 25 - LTS for that architecture on the Temurin releases page and follow the linked official macOS .pkg, Windows .msi (with the PATH and JAVA_HOME features named) or Linux packages guide (package temurin-25-jdk); install Maven from the official guide; then verify in a new terminal. It states that following the links needs network access, shows expected java -version, javac -version and mvn -v output with 'all three show 25' as the completion criterion, gives troubleshooting for 'command not found'/'is not recognized' and wrong-version cases with a clear stop-and-ask-your-instructor boundary, and ends with the IntelliJ IDEA install link, opening starter/pom.xml and a concrete check that Project Structure shows SDK 25. Remaining weaknesses in that path (Maven step without a completion check or Windows PATH route, stale lab README pointer, link-less Markdown companion) are recorded as new medium findings edu-install-design-001..003 rather than reopening this high.
